cross-006.answer: about 19% (4.8 ms of the 25 ms frame at 40 Hz)

cross-015.answer: Two Efforts are no longer active. Shader compile cache and build farm is completed: its end condition (every farm build reads from the cache) was met when dec-turn-the-shader-compile-cache-on-for-every-farm--4rr3b12b4sasdmaj was accepted on 2026-03-20. Co-op rollback netcode prototype is abandoned: dec-abandon-rollback-netcode-for-co-op--46envrg0v4pdwv7b was accepted on 2026-04-01, stopping rollback because re-running tides on every rolled-back frame costs 4.8 ms on Skiff.

netcode-004.answer: Rollback was abandoned because re-running the tide simulation on every rolled-back frame costs 4.8 ms on Skiff, about a fifth of the 25 ms frame, and the tide state must stay bit-for-bit deterministic (dec-abandon-rollback-netcode-for-co-op--46envrg0v4pdwv7b). The reason depends on the world Decision "Run the tide simulation in 32.32 fixed point" (dec-run-the-tide-simulation-in-32-32-fixed-point--c5rjfcnmhne4h05e), which keeps tides deterministic and so forces the re-simulation.

ports-012.answer: Saltglass caustic patterns shimmered badly in motion at the 540p floor (7 of 10 dune views, versus 2 of 10 at 576p), so the floor was raised to 576p in dec-raise-the-skiff-dynamic-resolution-floor-to-576p--fep9q7m08pp9f0bb, based on fnd-saltglass-caustics-shimmer-at-the-540p-floor--0aa8sts89vhq1s6q. The 576p decision has since been superseded by a later decision to lower the floor to 504p.

ports-013.answer: Ship Tern as Lantern's only upscaler

render-031.answer: Alpha-tested foliage cost 2.1 ms in the visibility buffer (its alpha test runs in the raster pass with a per-pixel texture fetch) versus 0.8 ms in forward+, and saltglass refracts the resolved scene so it cannot live in the buffer; see dec-visibility-buffer-for-opaque-geometry-foliage-an--gvnvp04jgm7kbfh9, derived from fnd-alpha-tested-foliage-costs-2-1-ms-in-the-visibil--f3g34x2k6fs367eb.

render-032.answer: Halcyon has no Skiff build, so shipping it would break the one-upscaler constraint, and the team wanted to own the upscaler code for saltglass rather than depend on vendor tickets and a license (Tern costs 0.7 ms more than Halcyon on Meridian). See dec-ship-tern-as-lantern-s-only-upscaler--fmreq35nzyjc7k4e.

render-046.answer: The cost finding that sank virtual shadow maps (3.1 ms) was a capture error; with cached pages VSM costs 1.4 ms, less than four cascaded shadow maps, and cascade seams through saltglass remained unsolved under CSM. (dec-use-virtual-shadow-maps-for-the-sun--x8nqkn9q7eaf1ap4)

render-047.answer: Because the release-build capture put the visibility buffer at 7.4 ms on Skiff against 8.1 ms for forward+ (6.3 ms with half-rate material resolve), so the forward+ fallback was no longer worth keeping, and maintaining two opaque paths cost about one engineer-week a month. Record: dec-visibility-buffer-on-all-platforms-skiff-resolve--k1ackk3c3275r5y1

world-036.answer: Kestrel retired the fiber scheduler because 41% of alpha crash reports had no usable stack, which blocked crash triage for beta, and a thread-pool prototype with continuation waits kept workers 93% busy during tide turns, close to the 95% fibers gave (dec-return-engine-jobs-to-a-thread-pool-with-continu--1zkc1v2x97taf50h).

world-051.answer: Float tides drifted apart between machines within 6 minutes, and integer adds and multiplies in 32.32 fixed point give the same bits on every CPU and compiler, so that drift cannot happen (record dec-run-the-tide-simulation-in-32-32-fixed-point--c5rjfcnmhne4h05e). The strict IEEE mode decision (dec-force-strict-ieee-float-mode-for-the-tide-simula--ecwmqt7ncjngysqw) was rejected in favor of it.

world-055.answer: Kelp stays because the decision `dec-shrink-kelp-s-dictionary-to-1-mb-for-streamed-as--yh8hktfqnyqhepew` ships a 1 MB Kelp dictionary and closes the reopened Zstandard option, since cold on Skiff Kelp still beats Zstandard, now by 1.25x after firmware 3.2 (`fnd-kelp-with-a-1-mb-dictionary-decodes-at-1-5-gb-s--y9v8jrxgbv6abrx5`).
